# Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist

Gothenburg, Sweden | +46 70 555 0808 | oskar.hl@example.com | GitHub: oskarhl-example

## Professional Summary
Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience building and maintaining web applications and backend services. Strong production experience with Node.js, TypeScript, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS and automated testing. Recent work includes developing onboarding services, integrating external APIs, improving frontend performance, and incrementally migrating an Express backend to NestJS. Fluent in English and experienced working in an on-call rotation.

## Technical Skills
- **Backend:** Node.js, NestJS, Express, REST APIs, GraphQL (maintaining a BFF), PHP, Laravel
- **Databases:** PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Firebase, Prisma, TypeORM
- **Cloud & CI/CD:** AWS (ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, CloudWatch, RDS), Docker, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Linux
- **Testing & Observability:** Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, Sentry, Datadog
- **Frontend:** TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, Angular, AngularJS, Vue, React Native
- **Other:** Python (basic; personal Home Assistant integrations), Terraform (small changes to existing files), Figma, Jira, Confluence, Unleash

## Professional Experience

### Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | Gothenburg
**2021–Present**
- Develop onboarding services and customer flows using React, TypeScript, Node.js/NestJS and PostgreSQL; deploy services on AWS ECS with GitHub Actions.
- Built a BankID identity-verification flow integrating the BankID API through a provider SDK, including QR-code and same-device flows, error states and retries. A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Built a secure document-upload service using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and SQS and PostgreSQL to track scan status.
- Helped migrate the onboarding backend incrementally from Express to NestJS, moving routes behind the same API gateway.
- Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds through code splitting, image optimisation, removing Moment.js, replacing a large charting library, and using Next.js SSR for landing pages.
- Contributed accessibility fixes to the onboarding flow in line with WCAG 2.1 AA, and migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite in 2023.
- Participate in the on-call rotation, one week every six weeks; maintain a GraphQL BFF with another developer.
- Collaborate with designers in Figma, interview candidates, and contribute across a six-person onboarding team. Acted as team lead for four months in 2024, covering 1:1s and sprint planning.
- The onboarding team received the internal Customer Impact Award in 2023.

### Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | Gothenburg
**2018–2021**
- Built websites and web applications for approximately 25 clients across retail, transport, local government and sports.
- Developed client applications using Angular, React and Vue, with Node.js/Express and PHP/Laravel backends; also built and maintained custom WordPress themes and plugins.
- Served as project tech lead and, with one other developer, built a React Native ferry-ticket app for purchasing and displaying tickets offline; the app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Set up GitLab CI for the agency, replacing a manual FTP-based deployment process.
- Worked with MySQL, MongoDB and Firebase across client projects.

### Web Developer | Nordkust Media AB | Gothenburg
**2014–2018**
- Developed newspaper websites and an AngularJS article editor using PHP, jQuery and MySQL.
- Implemented a paywall integration and worked on Varnish caching configuration and Ubuntu server administration.

### Freelance Developer / Student
**2012–2014**
- Built websites for friends, family, a local bakery and two bands using PHP, jQuery and WordPress.

## Selected Projects

### Express-to-NestJS Backend Migration | Älvgrind Fintech | 2021–2022
- Contributed to an incremental, route-by-route migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS behind the same API gateway.
- Presented the migration approach at a local JavaScript meetup in 2022.

### Home Assistant Integrations | Personal | 2022–Present
- Built two small custom home-automation integrations published on GitHub, with approximately 40 stars combined.
- Technologies: basic Python, YAML.

## Education
- **Bachelor in Computer Science**, West Coast University College (Högskola), Gothenburg | 2011–2014
- **Natural Science Programme**, Gymnasium | 2008–2011
- Additional learning: Advanced React Patterns (2022); AWS Cloud Practitioner course (2020; exam not taken); Coursera Machine Learning (2017; not completed)

## Additional Experience
- Mentor at a coding bootcamp in Gothenburg, 2019–2020.
- Speaker at a local JavaScript meetup in 2022: “Migrating Express to NestJS without stopping the world.”

## Languages
- Swedish: Native
- English: Fluent; used as a working language
- Arabic: Spoken at home; limited writing
- German: School-level

## Additional Information
- Driving licence: Category B
- References available on request

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear sections, relevant technical detail, quantified outcomes, and credible progression from web development to full-stack engineering and acting team leadership. The strongest evidence includes the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion improvement, 4.1s to 1.9s mobile LCP improvement, 50,000-download mobile app, AWS deployment experience, on-call participation, and the Express-to-NestJS migration. The document is substantially more professional and focused than the original source material. Its main content limitation is role positioning: it presents the candidate primarily as a broad full-stack developer, while the target role is a backend engineer expected to work mainly in Python. The CV also does not evidence PostgreSQL query tuning, database schema migrations, incident post-mortems, Kafka, or Kubernetes, although these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected that require removal.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, simple text formatting, conventional reverse-chronological experience, and strong keyword coverage for Node.js, NestJS, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, ECS, GitHub Actions, automated testing tools, CI/CD, English, on-call work, and transport-related experience. It should parse reliably. Its likely AI/ATS screening performance is strong for general backend or full-stack roles, but moderate for this specific vacancy because the highest-priority keyword is Python and the CV only mentions basic Python in a personal project. The document also lacks the exact terms query tuning, schema migrations, Kafka, Kubernetes, EKS, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, EDI, and shipment tracking. These should not be added as skills unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with REST API development, PostgreSQL, AWS deployment, Docker, GitHub Actions, automated testing, CI/CD, on-call work, production reliability, clear technical communication, and a transport-adjacent project. It also supports the company's ownership and pragmatic engineering signals through service ownership, incremental migration, performance work, accessibility improvements, and on-call participation. The primary requirement gap is 3+ years of professional Python backend experience or the specified comparable languages Go, Java, or Kotlin; the candidate's material only supports basic Python work in Home Assistant integrations and does not support three years of Python backend development. PostgreSQL experience is shown, but the candidate's material does not substantiate query tuning or database schema migrations. Kafka/event streaming, Kubernetes, the requested observability stack, and Dutch/French are also gaps. Logistics/transport exposure is shown through the ferry-ticket application, but not shipment tracking, freight forwarding, or EDI. English is shown through fluent working-language use and public technical presentation.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the backend relevance more prominent without implying Python experience. For example, change the opening to: "Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional web development experience, including production backend services with Node.js/TypeScript, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS." Retain the existing NestJS migration, API integration, testing, performance, and on-call details.
2. In the Professional Summary, explicitly connect the candidate's communication evidence to the role by changing the ending to: "Fluent in English, experienced explaining technical approaches through a JavaScript meetup presentation, and experienced in an on-call rotation." This is supported by the CV's English-language work and meetup talk.
3. In the Full-Stack Developer role at Älvgrind Fintech, revise the first bullet to use the job ad's backend terminology more directly while remaining truthful: "Develop backend onboarding services and customer flows with Node.js/NestJS, REST/API integrations, PostgreSQL and AWS ECS, alongside React and TypeScript frontend work; deploy through GitHub Actions." Do not state that the services are Python or FastAPI services.
4. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Cloud & CI/CD" to "Cloud, Deployment & CI/CD" and retain the existing AWS ECS, Docker, GitHub Actions and GitLab CI terms together. This improves matching for the ad's cloud deployment and CI/CD requirements.
5. In the Technical Skills section, change "Testing & Observability" to "Automated Testing & Observability". Keep Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, Sentry and Datadog exactly as listed; do not add Prometheus, Grafana or OpenTelemetry.
6. In the Selected Projects section, add the Ferry Ticket Mobile App as a short project or expand its existing agency bullet to include the transport keyword: "Built a React Native ferry-ticket application for purchasing and displaying tickets offline; project tech lead in a two-developer team; approximately 50,000 downloads." This is supported by the original candidate information and gives the CV stronger transport-domain relevance.
7. In the Education section, keep the AWS Cloud Practitioner course explicitly marked as "exam not taken" and the Coursera Machine Learning course as "not completed," as the current wording accurately avoids overstating credentials. No certification should be presented as earned.
